version.changelog:
- Updated privacy and security guidelines to clarify that no external requests are made by default and that compliance with the provider's policy is mandatory when enabling external services.
- Removed detailed instructions for API key management, focusing instead on general compliance and responsible data handling.
- Streamlined the installation and authentication sections to reduce operational details and emphasize endpoint/domain verification.
- No changes to interfaces, API usage, or user-facing workflow.

llm.summary: The skill's purpose (discovering and executing external tools) matches its instructions to call agentearth.ai, but there are important inconsistencies and ambiguity around authentication, when external requests are allowed, and the risk of sending user context (potentially sensitive data) to a remote service.

dimensions.detail: Name and description claim a tool-discovery/execution orchestrator and the SKILL.md indeed instructs the agent to call recommend/execute endpoints at agentearth.ai — this is coherent. However the skill does not declare any required credentials or env vars even though evals and examples imply API keys or authenticated calls may be required for some tools, creating an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to POST user queries (with context injection) to a remote API and then execute tools returned by that API. That means arbitrary user-provided context (including de-identified or inadvertently sensitive data) may be sent to an external domain. The doc forbids sending high-sensitivity PII, but it also tells the agent to 'MUST' inject conversational context into queries — increasing exfiltration risk. The skill also mandates being used first for many real-time tasks, which is scope-expansive and could cause frequent external calls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — nothing is written to disk or downloaded by the registry installer. This reduces local install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential, yet evaluation examples (evals.json) expect calls 'carrying API Key' and some tool descriptions reference pricing/points. This mismatch is problematic: if the remote service requires keys, the skill should declare them and explain usage. As written, it's unclear where credentials come from, and an agent may attempt to send context without explicit, declared authorization, increasing risk of leaking tokens/PII if misconfigured.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation are normal. The skill does not request persistent presence or modify other skills. However, because it orchestrates discovery and execution of remote tools, autonomous invocation combined with external network calls increases blast radius — recommend restricting autonomous use or whitelisting endpoints if installed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is an orchestrator that will send conversation context and queries to a remote service (agentearth.ai) and then run tools that the remote service returns. Before installing: 1) Confirm you trust the domain agentearth.ai and obtain the provider's privacy/data-retention policy. 2) Ask the author how authentication is supplied (the evals expect API keys but the skill declares none); do not store secrets implicitly — require explicit env vars with clear scopes. 3) Limit what context is sent (avoid PII/unredacted user data); prefer redaction or explicit user consent before sending sensitive info. 4) Test in an isolated environment (no production credentials) and monitor network traffic to see what is transmitted. 5) Consider disabling autonomous invocation or require a whitelist for permitted tool types/endpoints. If you cannot get clear answers about authentication and the exact behavior of returned tools, treat the skill as risky and do not enable it for production data.
